note: Entries with no oracle expression, and why; and the supported set itself.
Read sql/oracle/README.md first.
There is no percentage and no threshold here on purpose. A threshold is the
'broad set with hidden assumptions' this layer exists not to be: 94% coverage
is a number that sounds like progress and names nothing. Every supported entry
either has an expression that reaches it -- proved by a trace of Map::entry(),
not by a header claiming so -- or is listed below with a reason a person wrote.
`supported` is the denominator, recorded rather than recomputed. The gate used
to ask the code under test what it supported and then check the corpus reached
all of it -- so withdrawing an entry shrank supply and demand together and
'66 of 66 entries reached' stayed green while a function silently stopped being
translatable. That was the third way this gate was found lying. It is now
checked in both directions: an entry supported but not recorded is undeclared
support, one recorded but not supported has been withdrawn, and both are suite
errors until a person updates this file.
Refusals need nothing: a refusal has no semantics to check, it is the absence
of them. Only entries that are objects are counted.
`caveats_unwitnessable` is the other half of the same idea. A caveat says an entry may
disagree with SEL; the oracle now requires that somewhere it DOES, or that this file
says why it cannot. Inventing a caveat used to be free -- it silenced every check on
that entry and changed no output character -- and dropping a real one was invisible
wherever the comparator normalised the difference away.
`ansi-probe` is not a server. php/bin/sqlo registers it -- extends ansi, nothing
overridden -- so that the six ansi entries no shipped target resolves are
evaluated by one. It borrows PostgreSQL's connection because PostgreSQL is the
conformant engine of the four: SQLite's type affinity accepts almost any cast,
and MariaDB reads || as logical OR. Its supported set is smaller than any real
target's because ansi refuses most of what it declares.

mariadb.concat-null: Unwitnessable by construction, not by omission. It says concatenation yields NULL if an operand is NULL -- and SEL has no null, so the operand is a NONE and `N & "!"` is E_NO_SCALAR in SEL. There is no expression that puts SEL and the server on opposite sides of it: SEL has no answer to disagree with. Measured against the rows fixture's nullable `note` column. This is a refusal-class divergence wearing a caveat's clothes -- docs/SQL-TRANSLATION.md §11.2 is where it actually belongs -- and the caveat is kept because an application branching on Fragment::caveats still wants to be told.
mariadb.input-laxity: Unwitnessable for the same reason, one level up: it says the server accepts input SEL rejects. Where SEL rejects, SEL has no answer, so no expression can differ under it. DECODE_BASE64("aGVsbG8") -- unpadded -- is E_BAD_ARG in SEL and a value on the server, and since M5 the constant check refuses to translate it at all.

postgresql.regex-engine: Declared and not crossed. PostgreSQL's ARE anchors $ at end-of-string, so the trailing-newline expression that crosses this caveat on the MySQL family agrees here; and every other probe of the stated residue agreed too -- lazy quantifiers (a+?b), bounded repeats (a{2}), non-capturing groups ((?:ab)+) and alternation. Kept rather than removed because PCRE and POSIX ARE are different engine families and the subset SEL guarantees is the intersection of PCRE and ECMAScript, which is not what this server implements. Nobody has found the expression that separates them; that is a weaker statement than `they agree` and is the honest one.

ansi-probe.concat-null: Unwitnessable by construction, exactly as it is on every other dialect: it says concatenation yields NULL when an operand is NULL, and SEL has no null, so the operand is a NONE and the expression is E_NO_SCALAR in SEL. There is no expression that puts SEL and the server on opposite sides of it. The reasoning is the map's, not this dialect's, and is spelled out under mariadb above.
